title: Building America's Capacity to Innovate
author: P

Founder

From research and development to high-volume manufacturing, Intel is helping build the capacity America needs for the next era of innovation.

By: Naga Chandrasekaran, executive vice president and chief technology and operations officer, Intel Foundry

Semiconductors are so deeply integrated into our daily lives that most people do not even think about them. But they power the devices we carry, the cars we drive, the health care systems we rely on and the infrastructure that surrounds us all. Demand for computing power is growing at an unprecedented pace.

Meeting this demand requires some of the most advanced research and development (R&D), engineering and manufacturing work ever undertaken. Semiconductor manufacturing brings together breakthroughs in physics, materials science, chemistry and engineering at extraordinary precision and scale. It employs thousands of scientists, researchers, engineers, technicians and manufacturing professionals who work together to transform those breakthroughs into technologies used around the world.

While semiconductors have become increasingly central to modern life, the share manufactured in the United States declined from 37% to 10% between 1990 and 2022, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association.

For 250 years, America's ability to invent, develop and manufacture transformative technologies has helped drive global prosperity and progress. Semiconductor leadership will help determine whether America continues to do so for the next 250 years.
